name: Sparse and structured attention variants: NSA, DSA, and their honest deployment status
arithmetic_intensity: Sparse attention reduces the WORK SET but adds a full-context index pass and non-contiguous gather. NSA (Native Sparse Attention): three paths per query - compressed coarse tokens, top-k selected fine tokens, sliding window. Per-query decode work falls from L to (compressed_count + selected_count + w) while the index pass still touches all L. NSA reports 11.6x decode / 9.0x forward / 6.0x backward speedups at 64k context. But NSA names the trap: token-granular selection 'leads to the need to load a large number of individual tokens from the KV cache during attention computation. This non-contiguous memory access prevents efficient adaptation of fast attention techniques.' DSA (DeepSeek Sparse Attention, DeepSeek-V3.2): FP8-capable ReLU indexer scores every KV token, then only top-2048 are attended. Instantiated on MLA mode. The indexer is itself an attention-shaped pass over the full context. DSA's saving is a subtraction from the full-context, not a complexity class change.
scales_with: sparse selection granularity (block-granular is hardware-friendly; token-granular is not)
workarounds: Block-granular, group-shared sparse selection instead of per-token selection
FP8 indexers for the scoring pass
Grouped GEMM / flash-decoding style split-K over the selected set
Keep periodic full attention at a published ratio
notes: Deployment status: NSA is research-only (no production engine ships it). DSA is deployed in DeepSeek-V3.2 but requires FlashMLA on Blackwell. The key warning from NSA's own text: 'Many approaches fail to achieve speedups comparable to their theoretical gains' because of memory-access and scheduling, not arithmetic. For any sparse variant, the number to trust is measured decode tok/s at the target context length on the target part, not the complexity class. YOCO (self-decoder/cross-decoder) reduces cache size by sharing across layers with no math change - deployed in some models. RetNet: 8.4x decode and 70% memory saving at 8k on A100 - research-only. Kimi Linear: up to 75% KV reduction and 2.3x measured at 1M - research-only. Sources: arch-nsa, arch-yoco, arch-deepseek-v32-dsa, arch-retnet, arch-kimi-linear.
